# Nine Types of Men Every Woman Should Avoid

Everyone has a "type." Personally, I gravitate toward men with a prominent nose—bonus points if he sports a collection of acne scars reminiscent of Tommy Lee Jones. My friend Annie favors preppy men, but only once they've gone slightly to seed and developed a certain softness around the edges. Suzanne has a weakness for slender Japanese men who favor indie rock, while Maddy adores bike messengers regardless of shape or size.

But there exists a category of men who should be *nobody's* type—men defined not by charming quirks, but by an overabundance of genuinely undesirable qualities. Consider this your field guide to the men worth avoiding:

**1. The OverSharer**
The reigning champion of this category is Phillip Nobel, whose excruciatingly candid account of his extramarital affair appeared in *Elle*. The OverSharer will broadcast intimate details of your relationship to his mother, your mother, his blog readers, and anyone else within earshot willing to listen.

**2. The OverThinker**
One of the genuine pleasures of dating men is typically being spared lengthy, agonizing interrogations about what you *really* meant when you assured him those pants didn't make him look heavy. And yet, rare specimens exist who will spend hours dissecting even your most offhand remarks—parsing tone, subtext, and hidden implications with forensic intensity.

**3. The OverTalker**
Your friends remark that they've never seen you so quiet. That's because this man does enough talking for the both of you—and then some. When you finally manage to squeeze in a sentence, he interrupts and talks right over you anyway. You have two options: accept a future of perpetual silence, or say goodbye. The choice is yours.

**4. The OverDresser**
This dandy makes *Gossip Girl's* Chuck Bass look disheveled by comparison. That he requires more time than you to get ready is strike one; that his socks coordinate with his underwear *and* his ascot is what truly seals his fate.

**5. The OverEater**
It's an unfortunate truth that men can generally out-eat women. This particular specimen doesn't care. Food is his great love, and he'll press cannoli and baked ziti on you with the fervor of an overzealous Italian grandmother. Unless a future in stretch pants appeals to you, you may want to pass.

**6. The OverReactor**
Remember when Russell Crowe hurled a phone at a hotel clerk who'd somehow displeased him? That's this guy. From the elderly woman who accidentally bumps into him at the grocery store to the SUV that cuts him off on the highway, everyone in his path bears the brunt of his fury—you most of all. Don't walk away. Run.

**7. The Over-the-Topper**
He's the undisputed life of the party, perfectly willing to ride his motorcycle through a bar if he thinks it'll get a laugh. He's undeniably charming, but he simply never switches off—he's always "on." And that relentless energy quickly curdles into exhaustion.

**8. The OverAchiever**
Picture the male equivalent of Tracy Flick from *Election*, dressed in perfectly tailored jeans and a crisp white oxford, carrying a copy of his (naturally flawless) SAT scores in his wallet. Now try to imagine being intimate with him. You can't, can you?

**9. The OverCompensator**
Perhaps he was the least popular kid in his eighth-grade class, but that's no excuse for subjecting you to lengthy monologues about his income, his friends' envy over his new BMW, and how he could easily date supermodels if he simply chose to. Next!

# The Nine Male Archetypes Every Woman Should Steer Clear Of

We all gravitate toward certain physical or personality traits when it comes to romantic partners. I happen to find large noses attractive, especially when paired with weathered, scarred skin like Tommy Lee Jones has. My friend Annie goes for guys who used to be preppy but have since let themselves go and packed on some pounds. Suzanne falls for skinny Japanese men obsessed with indie music, and Maddy has a soft spot for bike messengers regardless of their build.

However, some male categories deserve universal rejection, characterized by having way too much of a negative trait. Consider this your roadmap for identifying men worth dodging:

**1. The Excessive Sharer**
Phillip Nobel exemplifies this category perfectly, having penned a cringe-worthy Elle article detailing his affair. This guy will spill your relationship's private moments to his mom, your mom, his blog followers, and basically anyone within earshot.

**2. The Excessive Analyzer**
One perk of dating men is typically avoiding lengthy interrogations about the true meaning behind your words. Still, occasionally you'll encounter someone who insists on picking apart your most casual remarks for hidden meanings, tone, and subtext.

**3. The Nonstop Talker**
Friends will remark that they've never seen you so silent — that's because this guy talks enough for the both of you, and then some more. On the rare occasion you manage to speak, he'll cut you off anyway. Your options: resign yourself to permanent silence, or walk away.

**4. The Fashion Obsessive**
This guy makes even Chuck Bass from Gossip Girl look disheveled. Taking longer than you to get dressed is bad enough, but coordinating his socks with his underwear and necktie? That's a dealbreaker.

**5. The Compulsive Eater**
Annoyingly, men naturally out-eat women, and this guy takes it further. Food is his true passion, and he'll shove pasta and desserts at you like an overzealous grandmother. Skip him unless you're prepared for a wardrobe full of elastic waistbands.

**6. The Hothead**
Think Russell Crowe hurling a telephone at a hotel employee. This guy erupts at everyone — the elderly woman who bumps his cart, the driver who cuts him off — and you'll bear the brunt of it most. Don't just leave; sprint.

**7. The Attention Hog**
He dominates every social gathering and would happily ride a motorcycle into a bar for laughs. He's charming initially, but his relentless need to perform gets exhausting fast, turning charisma into annoyance.

**8. The Perfectionist Achiever**
Imagine a male Tracy Flick from "Election" — pressed jeans, crisp shirt, SAT scores tucked in his wallet for reference. Now picture being intimate with him. Impossible, right?

**9. The Insecure Boaster**
He might have been awkward in middle school, but that's no excuse for endless bragging about his salary, his envy-inducing friends, or how he could land supermodels if he tried. Move along.

# When Good Traits Go Bad: The Universal Turn-Offs in Men

Everyone has their own unique checklist when it comes to what they find attractive in a partner. Some women swoon over a great sense of humor, while others prioritize ambition or kindness. However, dating experience—and no small amount of collective wisdom—reveals a truth that transcends personal preference: even admirable qualities become deeply unattractive once pushed to their extreme. What starts as an endearing trait can quickly curdle into something exhausting, embarrassing, or downright unbearable. Here are five archetypes that prove too much of anything is rarely a good thing.

## The OverSharer

There's something to be said for emotional openness, but the OverSharer takes transparency to an uncomfortable extreme. This is the man who treats his intimate relationship details as public content, broadcasting private moments to family members, friends, and anyone who happens to read his blog. Take the infamous case of Phillip Nobel, who publicly documented his own affair in excruciating detail for all to see. What should remain sacred between partners instead becomes fodder for public consumption, leaving anyone dating an OverSharer wondering what personal moment will become tomorrow's social media post or dinner party anecdote.

## The OverThinker

Thoughtfulness and emotional intelligence are attractive qualities—until they morph into obsessive overanalysis. The OverThinker cannot simply accept a comment at face value; instead, he dissects every word, tone, and pause for hidden meanings and secret implications. A casual "I'm tired tonight" becomes a two-hour investigation into whether his partner is losing interest, upset about something unspoken, or planning an exit strategy from the relationship. What should be simple, breezy conversations instead transform into exhausting interrogations, leaving his partner feeling like she needs to choose her words with the precision of a diplomat just to avoid triggering another spiral of analysis.

## The OverTalker

Confidence and the ability to carry a conversation can be genuinely appealing traits in a partner. But when confidence tips into domination, the result is the OverTalker—a man who treats every conversation as his personal monologue. He interrupts constantly, talks over his partner mid-sentence, and rarely pauses long enough to let her contribute a complete thought. Dates with the OverTalker often leave women feeling less like equal participants in a dialogue and more like a captive audience, nodding along while their own opinions, stories, and perspectives go unspoken and unheard.

## The OverDresser

Taking pride in one's appearance is admirable, and there's nothing wrong with a man who dresses well. But the OverDresser elevates grooming into an all-consuming obsession, coordinating every single accessory with meticulous, almost manic precision. Matching socks, underwear, and even ascots must align perfectly with the rest of his ensemble, as though he's perpetually preparing for a photo shoot rather than a casual dinner date. While style is attractive, this level of fastidiousness can come across as vanity taken to its logical extreme, leaving little room to wonder if there's substance beneath the perfectly curated surface.

## The Takeaway

While personal taste in partners will always vary widely, these five archetypes serve as a reminder that balance is key. The very traits that can make someone charming—openness, thoughtfulness, confidence, and self-care—become liabilities when taken to their extremes. The healthiest relationships thrive on moderation: honesty without oversharing, reflection without obsession, confidence without domination, and self-care without vanity. Recognizing these tipping points can help anyone navigate the dating world with a clearer sense of what genuinely enhances a relationship versus what ultimately undermines it.

# The 9 Types of Guys Who Are Giving "Red Flag" Energy (A Very Scientific Analysis)

Dating in your late twenties/early thirties is basically an anthropological field study, except instead of studying ancient civilizations, you're studying why the guy from the coffee shop mentioned his ex four times before asking your last name. After years of research (aka dates), countless brunches spent debriefing with my girlfriends, and one truly unhinged group chat that should probably be studied by scientists, I've identified nine distinct species of men who, despite their charms, are simply Too Much of One Thing. Think of this as a Pokédex, but for red flags.

## 1. The OverSharer

You know him. You've matched with him. He told you about his therapist, his childhood trauma, and his complicated relationship with his mother all before the appetizers arrived. Listen, emotional intelligence is attractive! Vulnerability is important! But there's a difference between "opening up" and "handing someone your entire unpacked baggage before they've even ordered a drink." I once had a first date where a man cried—actual tears—while explaining his fantasy football league drama. Sir, this is a Wendy's.

## 2. The OverThinker

This one analyzes texts like they're deciphering the Dead Sea Scrolls. "So when you said 'lol,' did you mean you actually laughed, or were you just being polite?" Buddy. I don't know. I barely remember sending that text. The OverThinker will spiral about a slightly-too-long response time, construct elaborate theories about your feelings based on punctuation, and generally exhaust everyone's emotional bandwidth trying to reassure him that no, you do not, in fact, hate him because you used a period instead of an exclamation point.

## 3. The OverTalker

Somewhere out there, a man is currently on a date, mid-monologue about the stock market, completely unaware that his date's soul has left her body approximately eleven minutes ago. The OverTalker doesn't ask questions because he doesn't need to—he's essentially podcasting at you. I once sat through a 45-minute uninterrupted explanation of blockchain technology. I still don't understand blockchain. I do, however, understand that I will never see that man again.

## 4. The OverDresser

Look, I appreciate effort. A well-fitted blazer? Sure. But when your date shows up looking like he's about to accept a Grammy for a genre that doesn't exist yet, something's off. The OverDresser wears more product in his hair than you do, has Views about pocket squares, and will absolutely comment if your outfit doesn't match the "vibe" of the restaurant he chose. This is a man who has spent more time on his outfit than on his personality development, and it shows.

## 5. The OverCompliment-er

"You're literally the most beautiful woman I've ever seen. You're an angel. I've never met anyone like you." Sir, we have known each other for six minutes. This feels like love bombing, and studies (my friend group chat) suggest that men who compliment excessively early on are often compensating for something—usually a complete lack of follow-through. Real recognition comes later, once you've actually shown personality traits worth complimenting.

## 6. The OverPlanner

He's already mapped out your third date, factored in your Myers-Briggs compatibility, and mentioned "meeting the parents" unprompted. There's confidence, and then there's a man who's basically building a spreadsheet of your future together before you've established whether you both like dogs. Slow down, Nostradamus.

## 7. The OverExplainer

Ask him what he does for work and prepare for a TED Talk. The OverExplainer cannot simply answer a question; he must contextualize it, provide background, offer three tangents, and circle back with a summary. Asking "how was your day?" should not require footnotes.

## 8. The OverConfident-in-His-Playlist Guy

He will make you a Spotify playlist. It will be 47 songs long. He will expect you to listen to all of it and have Opinions. This man believes his music taste is a personality trait and possibly a personality replacement.

## 9. The OverApologizer

The opposite extreme of confidence—this man apologizes for existing. He's sorry the restaurant is loud. Sorry he's five minutes late (he's not late). Sorry for breathing near you. While humility is nice, a man who cannot simply *be* without apologizing for taking up space becomes exhausting fast. You end up comforting him instead of enjoying your date.

---

At the end of the day, dating is about finding balance—someone who shares appropriately, dresses appropriately, and doesn't require you to co-sign a business plan by date three. The "Over" types aren't necessarily bad people; they're just... a lot. And sometimes "a lot" is exactly what makes an otherwise promising connection completely unsustainable. So here's to hoping your next match brings just the right amount of everything—confidence without ego, effort without desperation, and conversation without a syllabus.

# The Frisky: Where Everybody Found Their Voice

In the ever-evolving landscape of digital media, few platforms managed to capture the playful, honest spirit of modern relationships and pop culture quite like The Frisky. Launched as a response to the growing demand for content that spoke directly to readers about love, sex, and everyday life, the site quickly became a go-to destination for millions.

What made The Frisky stand out wasn't just its snappy headlines or celebrity gossip—though there was plenty of that. It was the way the platform managed to make everybody feel included in the conversation. Whether you were single and navigating the dating world, in a long-term relationship figuring out how to keep things interesting, or simply looking for validation that your weird quirks were actually pretty normal, The Frisky had something for you.

The site's tone was distinctly different from traditional women's magazines. It ditched the aspirational, unattainable lifestyle content in favor of something more relatable—messy, funny, and refreshingly honest. Writers shared personal stories about breakups, awkward first dates, and the reality of modern romance, creating a sense of community among readers who felt seen and understood.

Beyond relationship advice, The Frisky covered entertainment news with a wink and a nudge, always ready to poke fun at celebrity culture while still celebrating it. This balance of critique and genuine enthusiasm resonated with an audience tired of either mindless fan worship or cynical takedowns.

Perhaps what made The Frisky truly special was its democratic approach to content. Everybody's experiences mattered—there was no single "right" way to date, love, or live. This inclusive philosophy helped build a loyal readership that saw the site not just as entertainment, but as a genuine community.

Though media landscapes shift and platforms come and go, The Frisky's legacy lives on in how digital publications approach relationship content today: with humor, honesty, and an understanding that everybody deserves content that speaks to their real experiences, not just an idealized version of life.

# 9 Types of Guys to Swipe Left On (You'll Thank Us Later)

We've all been there: three dates deep, wondering how you ended up debating the ethics of crypto with a man who still has a Razr scooter in his living room "for aesthetic purposes." Save yourself the trouble. Here are nine red-flag archetypes to spot early.

**1. The Gym Mirror Selfie Guy**
His Instagram is 80% shirtless flexing, 20% motivational quotes about "grinding." He'll spend more time on his skincare routine than you will, and he *will* ask you to take "just one more" photo of him at the gym.

**2. The Perpetual Podcaster**
He doesn't have opinions—he has "takes he heard on a podcast yesterday." Ask him anything and get ready for a TED Talk you didn't sign up for, delivered with the confidence of a man who's never once been fact-checked.

**3. The "I'm Not Like Other Guys" Guy**
He'll tell you this unprompted, usually while doing something extremely like-other-guys, such as mansplaining wine to a sommelier or complaining about his ex to you on date one.

**4. The Ghost Who Reappears**
Vanishes for three weeks, then slides back in with "hey stranger 👀" like he didn't commit a full disappearing act. Bonus points if he acts confused about why you're not thrilled to hear from him.

**5. The Financial Mystery Man**
Drives a car worth more than your rent, lives with three roommates, and gets weirdly vague when you ask what he "does." Red flag, or reality TV pitch? You decide.

**6. The Serial Half-Texter**
Responds to novels with "lol" or a single emoji. Somehow still expects a relationship to bloom from these thrilling exchanges.

**7. The Self-Proclaimed Chef**
Can make exactly one pasta dish and will remind you of this fact at every dinner, unprompted, like he's auditioning for a Food Network special that will never happen.

**8. The Nostalgia Bro**
Peaked in high school and hasn't stopped talking about it since. Every story starts with "back when I played varsity..." Sir, it's been fifteen years.

**9. The Silent Treatment Strategist**
Uses disappearing acts as punishment instead of, you know, communicating like an adult. If a text delay gives him "the ick," run—don't walk.

---

**The bottom line?** Life's too short for lukewarm texts and men who peaked at prom. Hold out for someone who actually replies in full sentences. You deserve it. 💅

# 9 Types of Guys Every Woman Should Avoid (According to Every Rom-Com You've Ever Watched)

We've all been there — swiping, dating, wondering why our "situationship" feels like a bad sitcom plot. So let's break down the guy archetypes that pop culture has warned us about for decades. Consider this your public service announcement.

**1. The Ross Geller ("We Were On A Break!")**
He'll gaslight you into thinking you're the unreasonable one. Possessive, jealous, and somehow always the victim in his own story. Run.

**2. The Nate Jacobs (*Euphoria*)**
Charismatic on the surface, absolutely unhinged underneath. If your friends describe him as "intense" more than twice, that's not a compliment.

**3. The Chuck Bass (Season 1 era, before growth)**
Rich, magnetic, and treats women like acquisitions. Redemption arcs are for TV. In real life, red flags rarely turn into character development.

**4. The Barney Stinson**
Has a "playbook." Views dating as a game with rules only he knows. Charming until you realize the bit was never actually a bit.

**5. The Draco Malfoy (pre-redemption fanfic version)**
Negs you because he doesn't know how to process actual feelings. Cruelty isn't secretly longing — sometimes mean just means mean.

**6. The Jordan Catalano (*My So-Called Life*)**
Broody, unavailable, communicates in one-word sentences. Leaning against lockers is not a personality.

**7. The Christian Grey**
Mistakes control for intimacy and calls it romance. Red flags rebranded as "intensity." A contract is not a love language.

**8. The Joe Goldberg (*You*)**
The ultimate "he's just misunderstood" trap. Spoiler: the guy quoting poetry while stalking your Instagram is not swoon-worthy, he's a documentary waiting to happen.

**9. The Jim Halpert (Just Kidding — Keep This One)**
Actually, never mind. Jim's fine. We just wanted to see if you were still paying attention.

---

**Bottom line:** Fiction loves giving bad behavior a redemption arc and a soundtrack. Real life doesn't come with a season finale reset button. If you recognize a pattern from a screen, it's probably not "chemistry" — it's a character flaw.

---

Want me to adjust the tone (snarkier, more satirical, more feminist-critique-driven) or swap in different franchises (maybe more Marvel, reality TV, or musicians)?

# The Field Guide to "Over-" Boyfriends: A Survival Manual

So you've swiped right, gone on three dates, and now you're wondering if you've accidentally adopted a human golden retriever with commitment issues. Fear not! We've categorized the wild "Over-" Boyfriend species so you know exactly what you're dealing with.

## The OverTalker
**Mating call:** "So anyway, let me tell you about this one time in college..."

This man has never met a silence he didn't want to murder. He'll narrate his entire day, including the sandwich he ate for lunch (mayo side down, very important detail). Dating him means you'll know his opinions on everything from cryptocurrency to why Nolan's *Interstellar* "actually explains time travel correctly." You will never finish a sentence again. RIP your thoughts, 2019-present.

## The OverSharer
**Natural habitat:** Third date, unprompted trauma dump

He'll tell you about his ex, his therapist's professional opinion of his ex, and a detailed timeline of his last breakup complete with text message screenshots—all before the appetizers arrive. Emotional intimacy is great! Emotional information overload before you've picked a Netflix show together is a red flag wearing a name tag.

## The OverEater
**Distinctive marking:** Ordering "just an appetizer" then finishing yours too

Sweet, but you will never again enjoy a shared dessert. He orders the large, then side-eyes your fries like they owe him money. Dating him is a full commitment to portion control anxiety and pretending you're "not that hungry" so he can have seconds.

## The OverThinker
**Warning sign:** Texts you a 500-word essay analyzing why you used a period instead of an exclamation point

This man will spiral about whether "we should get drinks" means something deeper. He'll ask "but what did you MEAN by that" about your grocery list. Every decision—brunch spot, movie choice, whether to hold hands—becomes a TED Talk. Exhausting, but also weirdly makes you feel important? Concerning.

## The OverCompensator
**Signature move:** Revving the engine of his very reasonably-sized car

Buys you extravagant gifts on date two. Talks about his "business ventures" with suspicious vagueness. Somehow always needs to mention his gym PR unprompted. He's not overcompensating for anything specific, he just really wants you to know he's *fine*, everything's *fine*.

## The OverAchiever
**Mating call:** "I actually already have five-year, ten-year, and fifteen-year plans"

Impressive on paper, terrifying in practice. He color-codes his calendar including "spontaneous fun (7-9pm Thursdays)." Dating him means you're now also on a five-year plan, whether you agreed to it or not. Romance is a KPI to him now.

## The OverApologizer
**Distinguishing feature:** Says sorry for existing, specifically for taking up space on the sidewalk

He apologizes for apologizing. Bumps into a chair? Three-minute apology tour. You'll spend the relationship reassuring him he's not "too much" while gently wondering if you need a hobby that isn't emotional life support.

---

**The Verdict:** Every "Over-" boyfriend is really just a regular guy who forgot moderation exists. The good news? Balance can be taught. The bad news? You're not his mother, and dating shouldn't feel like a group project where you're doing all the work.

*Choose wisely, and always check if he over-texts before he over-commits.* 💅

# 5 Red-Flag Personality Types I've Officially Retired From My DMs

Okay, we need to talk. Not about you—about *them*. The men. The specific, recurring archetypes that keep showing up in different bodies but with the exact same personality disorder energy.

I've done the field research (extensively, unfortunately) so you don't have to. Let's get into it.

## 1. The "Motivational Speaker" Ex-Boyfriend

You know this guy. Gives off serious **early-2010s Tony Robbins-lite** energy. He doesn't just have opinions, he has *frameworks*. Everything is a "growth opportunity," including—especially—your feelings getting hurt.

**How to spot him:** He'll respond to "you hurt me" with "well what's the lesson here for you?"

Sir. I am not your TED Talk.

## 2. The Fake Himbo

This one's sneaky because himbos are supposed to be safe. But this guy uses "I'm just a simple guy" as a *personality shield* to avoid literally any accountability. He's got main character intelligence when it benefits him, golden retriever confusion when it doesn't.

Think: a man who can explain crypto for forty-five minutes but "just doesn't understand" why you're upset he forgot your birthday.

## 3. The Main Character Who Thinks You're an NPC

Gives **misunderstood-genius-in-his-own-biopic** vibes. Every conversation somehow becomes about his journey. You could be mid-crisis and he'll pivot to how *he* feels about *your* crisis.

He's not listening to you talk. He's waiting for his cue to bring it back to himself.

## 4. The "I'm Not Like Other Guys" Guy

This one actively campaigns against the very red flags he's currently waving. He'll preface bad behavior with "I'm just really honest" like honesty is a personality trait that excuses cruelty.

Spoiler: the guys who *are* different don't need to announce it. They just, you know. Are.

## 5. The Situationship Houdini

Emotionally available exactly until you need him to be. Master of the perfectly-timed disappearing act, always right when things get real. Shows back up with a "hey stranger 👀" text like nothing happened.

The audacity. The confidence. The absolute chaos.

---

**The takeaway?** None of this is about hating men—it's about knowing the patterns so you stop mistaking a red flag parade for a personality. You deserve someone who isn't a walking cautionary tale.

# 7 Dating Disasters You'll Recognize (And How to Spot Them Before It's Too Late!)

We've all been there, girls—three dates in, butterflies fluttering, and then suddenly he's asking to "borrow" your rent money or comparing you to his ex... again. Before you swipe right one more time, check out our field guide to the most notorious dating archetypes plaguing singles everywhere!

## 1. The Peter Pan

**Spot him by:** His apartment still has his college roommate's futon, and he refers to his mom doing his laundry as "she just likes to help out!"

This guy hasn't met a responsibility he couldn't dodge. Think Vince Vaughn in basically every early-2000s rom-com—charming, hilarious, and allergic to commitment. He'll plan the *best* spontaneous road trip you've ever been on, but don't expect him to remember your birthday.

**Warning sign:** He calls his car "she" and treats her better than his last three girlfriends combined.

## 2. The Almost-Famous

**Spot him by:** "I basically wrote that song" and "my screenplay is in development" (it is not in development).

He's got a MySpace... we mean Instagram full of blurry backstage photos and big dreams. He'll talk about his "big break" over a drink that you paid for.

**Warning sign:** He name-drops someone "in the industry" within the first ten minutes of meeting you.

## 3. The Emotionally Unavailable Poet

**Spot him by:** Deep stares, brooding silences, and a suspicious number of journals.

This is your Mr. Big archetype, ladies. He'll say things like "I'm just not good at this" while still very much doing "this" for six more months. He communicates primarily through meaningful eye contact and vague texts sent at 1am.

**Warning sign:** He's quoted Fight Club unironically more than once.

## 4. The Try-Hard Alpha

**Spot him by:** Talks over you at dinner, sends his food back twice, tips 10% and calls it "generous."

This one struts in like he's auditioning for a cologne commercial. He needs you to know he's "not like other guys," which, ironically, makes him exactly like every other guy in this category.

**Warning sign:** He has opinions about your order before the waiter even arrives.

## 5. The Serial Almost-Boyfriend

**Spot him by:** Somehow you've met his friends, stayed over four nights a week, and yet when someone asks "are you guys together?" he laughs nervously.

He'll give you all the perks of a relationship with none of the labels. Basically the human embodiment of "it's complicated."

**Warning sign:** His last relationship also lasted "informally" for two years.

## 6. The Nostalgia Junkie

**Spot him by:** Can't stop talking about his ex—her name comes up more than yours does on a good day.

Whether it's comparing your cooking, your laugh, or worse, your *actual personality* to what's-her-face, this guy hasn't logged off from his last relationship, even if he swears he's "totally over her."

**Warning sign:** He still has her as an emergency contact "just in case."

## 7. The Chronically Online Charmer

**Spot him by:** Perfect texter, terrible in person. All those clever one-liners? Yeah, he definitely ran them by his group chat first.

He'll have you giggling at 11pm over witty banter, but when you finally meet up, the conversation dies faster than a Nokia battery circa 2003.

**Warning sign:** He's better at flirting via AIM away messages (metaphorically speaking) than actual eye contact.

---

**The bottom line, ladies?** Life's too short for anything less than a leading man. So grab your girlfriends, a bottle of Chardonnay, and remember: you deserve a real rom-com ending, not a made-for-TV rerun. 💋
